questions.question: Which of the following physical properties of water is scientifically accurate? (FBISE 2025 Model)

options.A: Boils at 100°C at standard 1 atm pressure
options.D: Contracts when it freezes into ice

questions.explanation: Water has a boiling point of 100°C at 1 atm, high heat of vaporization (40.7 kJ/mol), high heat of fusion (6.01 kJ/mol), and uniquely expands when freezing due to an open cage-like hydrogen-bonded crystal lattice.

questions.question: Why does ice float on the surface of liquid water, thereby insulating aquatic ecosystems in freezing winters? (FBISE 2024-II)

options.A: Ice has a higher density than liquid water
options.B: Ice has a lower density ($0.917\text{ g cm}^{-3}$) than liquid water ($1.00\text{ g cm}^{-3}$) at 0°C

questions.explanation: In ice, each water molecule is tetrahedrally hydrogen-bonded in an open hexagonal lattice with empty spaces, giving it a density (~0.917 g/cm³) lower than liquid water (1.00 g/cm³). Therefore, ice floats.

questions.question: At what temperature does liquid water attain its maximum density ($1.00\text{ g cm}^{-3}$)? (FBISE 2023-II)
questions.explanation: Water exhibits anomalous expansion between 0°C and 4°C. As ice melts and reaches 4°C, hydrogen-bonded cage structures collapse, packing molecules most tightly at 4°C where density reaches maximum ($1.000\text{ g cm}^{-3}$).

questions.question: Which metal ions dissolved in water are primarily responsible for causing water hardness? (FBISE 2022-I, 2024-I)
questions.explanation: Water hardness is caused by dissolved multivalent cations, primarily calcium ($Ca^{2+}$) and magnesium ($Mg^{2+}$) ions, in the form of bicarbonates, sulphates, and chlorides.

questions.question: Temporary hardness of water is caused by the presence of dissolved: (FBISE 2021-I, 2023-I)
questions.explanation: Temporary hardness is exclusively caused by dissolved calcium hydrogen carbonate ($Ca(HCO_3)_2$) and magnesium hydrogen carbonate ($Mg(HCO_3)_2$), which can be precipitated by simple heating.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds causes permanent hardness in water? (FBISE 2020-II)
questions.explanation: Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved sulphates and chlorides of calcium and magnesium ($CaSO_4, MgSO_4, CaCl_2, MgCl_2$), which cannot be removed by boiling.

questions.question: In Clark's method for removing temporary hardness of water, which chemical reagent is added in calculated quantity? (FBISE 2019-II, 2022-II)
questions.explanation: Clark's method removes temporary hardness on a municipal scale by adding a calculated quantity of slaked lime: $Ca(HCO_3)_2 + Ca(OH)_2 \to 2CaCO_3\downarrow + 2H_2O$.

questions.question: Which chemical is used to remove both temporary and permanent hardness from water on an industrial scale? (FBISE 2018-I, 2021-II)
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate ($Na_2CO_3$, washing soda) removes both temporary and permanent hardness by precipitating soluble $Ca^{2+}$ and $Mg^{2+}$ ions as insoluble carbonates ($CaSO_4 + Na_2CO_3 \to CaCO_3\downarrow + Na_2SO_4$).

questions.question: The ion-exchange resin (Zeolite) method removes water hardness by exchanging $Ca^{2+}$ and $Mg^{2+}$ ions for: (FBISE 2017-I, 2020-I)
questions.explanation: Sodium zeolite (sodium aluminum silicate, $Na_2Z$) exchanges its loosely held $Na^+$ ions for $Ca^{2+}$ and $Mg^{2+}$ ions in hard water: $Na_2Z + Ca^{2+} \to CaZ + 2Na^+$. The resin is regenerated using concentrated $NaCl$ brine.

questions.question: When soap is used in hard water, an insoluble curdy precipitate (scum) forms because soap reacts with $Ca^{2+}$ or $Mg^{2+}$ to form: (FBISE 2016-II, 2019-I)
questions.explanation: Soap is soluble sodium stearate ($C_{17}H_{35}COONa$). In hard water, $Ca^{2+}$ replaces $Na^+$, precipitating insoluble greyish calcium stearate scum: $2C_{17}H_{35}COONa + Ca^{2+} \to (C_{17}H_{35}COO)_2Ca\downarrow + 2Na^+$.

questions.question: The thick crusty deposit formed inside steam boilers and hot water pipes from hard water is called: (FBISE 2015-I)
questions.explanation: Boiler scales are insoluble deposits of $CaCO_3$ and $CaSO_4$. Being poor thermal conductors, they waste fuel and cause localized overheating that can lead to catastrophic boiler explosions.

questions.question: Water is recognized as a 'universal solvent' primarily due to: (FBISE 2014-II, 2018-II)

options.A: Its high polarity and extensive hydrogen bonding capacity

questions.explanation: Water possesses a bent polar geometry ($H-O-H$ angle 104.5°) with high electronegativity difference ($O=3.5, H=2.1$) and high dielectric constant (~80), allowing it to hydrate, separate, and dissolve ionic and polar substances.

questions.question: Which of the following acute gastrointestinal bacterial infections is a deadly waterborne disease spread by drinking water contaminated with sewage containing Vibrio cholerae? (FBISE 2021-I)
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae transmitted through drinking water contaminated with human fecal waste, causing severe watery diarrhea, rapid dehydration, and shock.

questions.question: Excessive agricultural runoff carrying synthetic nitrate and phosphate fertilizers into lakes causes explosive algal growth known as: (FBISE 2017-II)
questions.explanation: Eutrophication occurs when excess nutrient runoff ($N$ and $P$) stimulates rapid algal blooms. As the algae die, aerobic decomposition by bacteria strips dissolved oxygen from the water, suffocating fish.

questions.question: Prolonged consumption of groundwater containing excessive concentrations of fluoride ions ($>1.5\text{ mg/L}$) leads to: (FBISE 2016-I, 2023-II)

options.A: Fluorosis (mottling of teeth and skeletal deformities)

questions.explanation: Excess fluoride damages ameloblasts during tooth development, resulting in dental fluorosis (mottled brown enamel) and skeletal fluorosis (crippling joint and bone calcification).

questions.question: Which of the following heavy metal contaminants in industrial wastewater causes severe neurological disorders and kidney damage? (FBISE 2019-I)
questions.explanation: Heavy metals such as lead ($Pb$), mercury ($Hg$), cadmium ($Cd$), and arsenic ($As$) are bioaccumulative systemic poisons that damage the brain, central nervous system, and kidneys.

questions.question: What chemical disinfectant is universally added to municipal drinking water supplies to kill pathogenic bacteria and microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Chlorination ($Cl_2 + H_2O \rightleftharpoons HOCl + HCl$) produces hypochlorous acid ($HOCl$), an effective oxidizing bactericide that destroys microbial cell membranes.

questions.question: Typhoid fever is a dangerous waterborne infection caused by which bacterium?
questions.explanation: Typhoid is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi, transmitted via water or food contaminated with human feces, causing prolonged high fever, intestinal ulceration, and delirium.

questions.question: Why cannot temporary hardness of water be removed by adding common salt ($NaCl$)?

options.A: $NaCl$ does not precipitate calcium or magnesium ions

questions.explanation: $NaCl$ contains $Na^+$ and $Cl^-$ ions, neither of which forms an insoluble precipitate with $Ca^{2+}$ or $Mg^{2+}$ ions. It cannot remove hardness.

questions.question: A chemical reaction that occurs during the boiling of temporary hard water containing calcium bicarbonate is:
questions.explanation: Heating causes the thermal decomposition of soluble calcium bicarbonate into insoluble calcium carbonate precipitate ($CaCO_3$), water, and carbon dioxide gas, softening the water.

questions.question: What is the specific heat capacity of pure liquid water, giving it high thermal buffering capacity?
questions.explanation: Water has an unusually high specific heat capacity of $4.184\text{ J g}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$ (or $1\text{ cal g}^{-1\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$), allowing it to absorb or release large amounts of heat with minimal temperature change, stabilizing Earth's climate.

questions.question: Which of the following organic pollutants present in untreated sewage causes extensive water pollution and foul odor upon anaerobic decomposition?

options.A: Human fecal matter, domestic waste food, and synthetic detergents

questions.explanation: Domestic sewage contains organic compounds (proteins, carbohydrates, fats, detergents) that undergo anaerobic decay by microorganisms, generating foul-smelling $H_2S$, $NH_3$, and methane.

questions.question: Amoebic dysentery is caused by which pathogenic waterborne parasite?
questions.explanation: Amoebic dysentery is caused by the protozoan parasite Entamoeba histolytica, ingested through fecal-contaminated drinking water, leading to severe colon inflammation and bloody stool.

questions.question: What type of intermolecular force accounts for water's unusually high boiling point (100°C) compared to $H_2S$ ($-60^\circ\text{C}$)?
questions.explanation: Extensive hydrogen bonds form between the highly electronegative oxygen atom of one water molecule and the electropositive hydrogen atoms of adjacent molecules, requiring significant thermal energy to break.

questions.question: Which of the following synthetic compounds in detergents causes persistent foam pollution in rivers because they resist bacterial biodegradation?
questions.explanation: Detergents with branched hydrocarbon chains cannot be metabolized by aquatic microorganisms, resulting in long-lasting toxic foam blankets on surface waters that inhibit aeration.

questions.question: In the sodium zeolite water softening process, when the zeolite resin ($Na_2Z$) is completely exhausted, how is it chemically regenerated?

options.A: By washing with a concentrated aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine)
options.C: By treating with concentrated nitric acid

questions.explanation: Passing concentrated $NaCl$ (brine) over exhausted $CaZ$ drives the reverse ion-exchange reaction ($CaZ + 2NaCl \to Na_2Z + CaCl_2$), regenerating active $Na_2Z$ for continued use.

questions.question: Which viral waterborne disease primarily attacks the liver and is spread through drinking fecal-contaminated water?
questions.explanation: Hepatitis A and E viruses are transmitted via the fecal-oral route through contaminated drinking water, causing acute liver inflammation, jaundice, and fatigue.

questions.question: Why is distilled water considered soft water?

options.A: It is free of dissolved calcium and magnesium mineral ions

questions.explanation: Distillation evaporates water and condenses pure vapor, leaving non-volatile calcium, magnesium, and other mineral salts behind, rendering distilled water free of hardness.

questions.question: What is the biological consequence when dissolved oxygen (DO) levels in a freshwater lake fall below $4\text{ mg/L}$ due to pollution?

options.A: Fish and other aerobic aquatic organisms die from suffocation

questions.explanation: Game fish and diverse aquatic organisms require at least 4–6 mg/L of dissolved oxygen. When DO falls below this threshold, fish suffer hypoxia, suffocate, and die en masse.

questions.question: Cryptosporidiosis is a severe diarrheal waterborne disease caused by Cryptosporidium, which is a:
questions.explanation: Cryptosporidium is a microscopic protozoan parasite whose protective thick-walled oocysts survive conventional chlorine disinfection, requiring filtration or UV treatment to remove.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is an effective coagulant added to municipal water treatment plants to aggregate colloidal clay impurities into settling flocs?
questions.explanation: Alum (aluminum sulphate, $Al_2(SO_4)_3$) hydrolyzes in water to form gelatinous aluminum hydroxide ($Al(OH)_3$) precipitate that traps and settles suspended clay and bacteria.

questions.question: Water has an unusually high surface tension due to:

options.A: Strong cohesive hydrogen bonds between surface water molecules
options.D: Van der Waals forces between gas molecules

questions.explanation: Molecules at the liquid water surface experience net inward attractive hydrogen bonding from neighboring molecules below, creating a high surface tension that supports water striders.

questions.question: Which test can rapidly distinguish between hard water and soft water in a laboratory?

options.A: Shaking equal volumes of each sample with standard soap solution and observing lather height
options.C: Measuring boiling point with a clinical thermometer

questions.explanation: Soft water produces a rich, stable lather immediately when shaken with soap solution, whereas hard water forms a cloudy insoluble curd (scum) with minimal or no lather.

questions.question: What is the primary industrial application of soft water in thermal power plants?

options.A: Boiler feedwater to prevent scale formation and boiler explosion hazards
options.B: To create soap foam in engines

questions.explanation: High-pressure industrial boilers require demineralized soft water to avoid deposits of $CaCO_3$ and $CaSO_4$ scale, which cause localized overheating and tube rupture.

questions.question: Which pesticide group used in agriculture bioaccumulates through aquatic food chains, causing eggshell thinning in predatory birds?
questions.explanation: Persistent organochlorine pesticides like DDT are fat-soluble and resist metabolic breakdown, magnifying in concentration at each trophic level (biomagnification) and interfering with calcium deposition.
